skill.name: playwright-skill
skill.description: Use Playwright to automate browser checks, run generated scripts, detect local dev servers, capture screenshots, and validate web flows.
skill.summary: Automates browser testing and visual checks with Playwright scripts.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most documentation backtick and example URL detections are false positives. Material risks remain in run.js, which executes generated JavaScript with Node privileges and can install dependencies automatically. Header injection and sandbox-disabled browser launch also need remediation before marketplace auto-install.

remediation.issue: Universal executor runs generated JavaScript with local Node.js privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Replace require-based execution with a constrained Playwright runner, or require explicit user confirmation and sandbox generated code.

remediation.issue: run.js automatically runs npm and npx commands when Playwright is missing.
remediation.suggestion: Move dependency installation to an explicit setup step, pin dependencies with a lockfile, and avoid auto-install during execution.

remediation.issue: Custom header environment variables can be sent to every browser context.
remediation.suggestion: Scope injected headers to approved origins and warn users before using credential-bearing header values.

remediation.issue: Chromium launches with sandbox-disabling flags by default.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --no-sandbox defaults and make sandbox disabling an opt-in compatibility setting.

remediation.issue: Executable temp files are written inside the skill directory and cleaned later.
remediation.suggestion: Create temp files in the operating system temp directory, restrict accepted script paths, and remove files after execution.

content.value_statement: Manual browser checks are slow and easy to miss. This skill creates focused Playwright automation for pages, forms, screenshots, and responsive checks.
actual_capabilities: Detects common localhost development servers before browser tests run.
Runs custom Playwright scripts from files, inline input, or standard input.
Launches Chromium, Firefox, or WebKit through reusable helper functions.
Tests pages, forms, login redirects, links, and responsive layouts.
Captures screenshots and extracts visible text or table data.
Applies optional HTTP headers from documented environment variables.
limitations: Requires Node.js, Playwright, and browser dependencies on the local machine.
Generated scripts can execute local code and should be reviewed before sensitive tasks.
External sites, credentials, and production targets need explicit user approval.
Screenshots and browser checks do not replace full application test coverage.

use_cases.title: Check a Local Web App
use_cases.description: Detect a running dev server, open the app, capture screenshots, and report visible layout issues.

use_cases.title: Validate User Workflows
use_cases.description: Exercise login, form submission, navigation, and redirect flows with focused Playwright automation.

use_cases.title: Inspect Responsive Behavior
use_cases.description: Compare desktop, tablet, and mobile views and summarize visible regressions from saved screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Local Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my running dev server and test the home page in a visible browser. Capture a screenshot and report visible layout issues.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Form Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to fill the contact form, submit it, and report validation messages and success states. Ask before using real credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Responsive Views
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a responsive check across desktop, tablet, and mobile widths. Save screenshots and summarize layout regressions with file paths.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Focused Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright script for [workflow] against [URL]. Keep the URL configurable and explain external requests before running it.

output: Found one local server on port 3001.
Loaded the home page in a visible Chromium window.
Saved desktop and mobile screenshots and noted two layout issues.

output_examples.input: Test whether login redirects to the dashboard.
output_examples.output: The login form submitted successfully and redirected to the dashboard. The script reported no visible error messages.

output: Collected external links from the page.
Reported working and failing links with their status codes.
Flagged links that timed out during the check.

best_practices: Review generated scripts before execution when credentials, uploads, or external domains are involved.
Use localhost or staging targets unless the user explicitly approves production testing.
Keep URLs and secrets configurable and scoped to the tested origin.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated automation against unknown external sites without user approval.
Do not place long-lived credentials in broad PW_EXTRA_HEADERS values.
Do not treat visual screenshots as proof that business logic is correct.

faq.question: Does this skill require Playwright to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The setup command installs Playwright and browser binaries when they are missing.

faq.question: Can it test a local development server?
faq.answer: Yes. It probes common localhost ports and asks when more than one server is found.

faq.question: Can it test external websites?
faq.answer: Yes, but provide the URL and approve any sensitive credentials or production actions first.

faq.question: Where are generated scripts stored?
faq.answer: The instructions direct generated Playwright scripts and screenshots to temporary paths under /tmp.

faq.question: Does it run in a visible browser?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for visible browser runs by default unless headless mode is requested.

faq.question: Is this safe for secrets?
faq.answer: Use caution. Header variables can send credential values to pages that the browser visits.
